generators.lens: Unconventional approaches. Reframe the problem, borrow mechanisms from unrelated domains, combine things nobody combines. Novelty never excuses ignoring the stated constraints.
Start from a concrete, recurring pain: who exactly has it, when, how often, and how they cope today. The solution must follow from that pain, not the other way round.
Demand and sustainability. Why people would adopt it and keep using it, how the first users are reached, and how it sustains itself (operations, revenue, cost) after the first version.

judges.lens: Can this actually be built and run within the stated team, time and budget? Hunt for hidden costs: data acquisition, external APIs, regulation, operations, cold start, maintenance.
Is the problem worth solving, and what is genuinely new compared with existing alternatives (products, communities, manual workarounds)? Expose repackaged existing things.

criteria.description: How painful, frequent and widespread the problem is, and how much the idea actually relieves it.
How new the approach is, not just the packaging.
Buildable and operable within the stated constraints.
How quickly and cheaply the core hypothesis can be validated with a first version.
A clear reason to choose this over existing alternatives.

fieldHints.title: Product / service name
fieldHints.oneLiner: One sentence: what it is and for whom
fieldHints.firstSteps: Core feature of the first version / first experiment

generators.lens: Bold questions at the edge of the field. Unexpected connections between literatures, methods or datasets. Aim for questions that would change what people believe.
Questions that can be answered cleanly: identifiable effects, obtainable data, sound designs, clear falsification criteria. Prefer a sharp answer to a vague big question.
Start from consequences. Questions whose answers matter to practitioners, policy, or adjacent fields, and say who would act differently given the result.

judges.lens: Validity, identification, confounds, sample size, data access, ethics approval, and whether the timeline and skills are realistic.
Significance and novelty relative to existing literature. Would the relevant community care? Flag questions that are already answered or trivially answered.

criteria.description: How much the answer would matter to the field or to practice.
Not already answered; a genuinely new question or method.
Soundness of the design; ability to produce a trustworthy answer.
Data, resources, skills and time available under the constraints.
Well-posed and falsifiable; clear what result would count as an answer.

fieldHints.title: Working title of the study
fieldHints.oneLiner: The research question in one sentence
fieldHints.problem: The gap in knowledge and why it matters
fieldHints.audience: Who cares about the answer (community, practitioners, decision-makers)
fieldHints.differentiation: How it differs from prior work (claim only what you are sure of)

marketing.label: Campaigns, content, brand, growth, launch ideas

generators.lens: Attention-grabbing, unexpected concepts. Cultural hooks, formats nobody in the category uses, ideas people would talk about.
Start from a sharp audience insight: a tension, habit, or unspoken truth. Build the message from that insight.
Channels, funnels and measurable outcomes. How the idea spreads, what it costs per result, and how it is tested and iterated.

judges.lens: Brand fit, quality of the audience insight, clarity and memorability of the message, reputational risk.
Reach, cost, executability with the stated budget and team, measurability, speed to learn.

criteria.description: Rooted in a real insight about the target audience.
Stands out in the category; memorable.
The audience gets the point immediately.
Doable with the stated budget, team and timeline.
Clear success metrics; can be tested small before scaling.

fieldHints.title: Campaign / concept name
fieldHints.audience: Target audience and the insight about them
fieldHints.differentiation: How it differs from what competitors and the category usually do

strategy.label: Business strategy, decisions, policy, process and organization improvements

generators.lens: Reframe the goal and challenge the assumptions behind it. Options that change the game rather than optimize the current one.
Pragmatic, incremental options that can be executed with existing people, systems and budget, starting next week.
Start from the people affected: incentives, likely resistance, fairness, second-order effects. Options that people will actually adopt.

judges.lens: Execution risk, cost, dependencies, reversibility, failure modes, legal and compliance exposure.
Size and durability of the effect on the stated goal, strategic coherence, opportunity cost.

criteria.description: Size and durability of the effect on the goal.
Executable with available people, systems, budget and time.
Higher score = lower or better-managed downside; reversible if it fails.
Effect relative to money, time and attention spent.
Likelihood that the affected people adopt and support it.

fieldHints.differentiation: How it differs from the status quo and the obvious alternatives

creative.label: Stories, games, events, art, shows, content series, names, concepts

generators.lens: Surprising premises, genre collisions, bold formal choices. Ideas that make people say 'I have never seen that'.
Structure and execution: coherent worlds, characters, mechanics, pacing. Ideas that hold up when developed in depth.
What the target audience will feel, share and come back for. Emotional payoff first, then the form that delivers it.

judges.lens: Originality, artistic coherence, emotional depth. Call out clichés and derivative work.
Producibility with the stated resources, audience appeal, scope risk, what it would take to ship.

criteria.description: Fresh premise or form; not derivative.
Makes the audience feel something strong.
Internally consistent; holds up when developed.
The intended audience would seek it out and share it.
Can be made with the stated resources and time.

general.label: Anything else: life, learning, education, community, personal projects, mixed topics

generators.lens: Unexpected angles and reframings. Question the premise of the topic; borrow from far-away domains.
Start from the people involved: what they actually do, feel and struggle with today. Ideas that fit real behavior.
Simple, cheap, robust ideas that work with what is already available and can be tried immediately.

judges.lens: What could go wrong, what is unrealistic, what is being assumed without evidence, what it really costs.
How much good the idea could do, how new it is, what it could grow into.

criteria.description: How much it helps with the stated goal.
Fresh compared with the obvious answers.
Doable under the stated constraints.
Can be tried small and judged quickly.
Still works when things do not go as planned.
